entities.summary:
Jan van Essen and Hendrik Vos, the first two Lutheran martyrs, were executed by the Council of Brabant in Brussels on 1 July 1523. 

These two men, who adhered to the Reformation doctrine, played a pivotal role in shaping the religious landscape of Europe during the tumultuous years of the early 16th century. 

Their sacrifice had a profound impact on the development of Protestantism, inspiring others to stand against the Catholic Church's authority. The legacy of Jan van Essen and Hendrik Vos continues to be felt today, with their story serving as a powerful symbol of the courage and conviction required to challenge established power structures.

The execution of Jan van Essen and Hendrik Vos in 1523 is a testament to the intense religious tensions that characterized the early modern period. The events surrounding their deaths served as a catalyst for the Protestant Reformation, which would go on to shape the course of Western history.
